The test image shows a soybean **pod** being held — yellowish/tan at maturity with distinct dark brown-black irregular blotches/lesions on the pod surface. This narrows candidates to pod-affecting diseases: **Diaporthe**, **Anthracnose**, **Phomopsis**.

Let me view reference images for top candidates in parallel.
The Anthracnose reference (bottom-left panel) shows very similar dark irregular blotches on a tan/hairy mature pod — closely matching the test image. Let me view a few more to confirm.
I need at least 12 reference images. Let me view more.

I've now viewed 14 reference images. My analysis is clear.

**Summary of findings:**
- **Test image**: Soybean pod held in hand, yellowish-tan (mature), with prominent dark brown-black irregular blotches concentrated on the pod surface, hairy pod texture.
- **Anthracnose** reference (bottom-left panel): shows a virtually identical tan/hairy mature pod with the same dark irregular blotching pattern — best match.
- **Diaporthe**: mostly stem symptoms; pod shows small black pycnidia in linear rows, not large blotches.
- **Phomopsis**: pods show circular pycnidia patterns / chalky white mold — different pattern.
- **White Mold**: white cottony mycelium on pods — not present.
- All other candidates (leaf diseases, root/stem diseases) don't involve pod blotching symptoms.

The dark irregular blotches on the mature hairy pod are characteristic of Anthracnose, which causes "black fungal bodies on infected pods."

Diaporthe would show linear rows of small pycnidia; Phomopsis would show circular pycnidia or chalky white mold; White Mold would show cottony mycelium. The large irregular dark blotching on the pod exterior is characteristic of Anthracnose stem blight affecting pods."}
